shape.before: Repeated smooth oval crab body, small non-specific projections, thin rod-like walking limbs and two simple paddle tips; no species-specific ventral structure.
shape.changed: Broad low outline with nine authored anterolateral teeth per side including long lateral spines; two frontal cues; smaller eyes; elongated ridged chelae with selected female rust fingers; six plated pointed walking limbs and separate articulated P5 chains with flattened propodus and oval terminal blade. Broad female apron with narrowed telson cue and transverse creases.
shape.remaining: Proportions and tooth placement are not specimen measurements. Mouthparts, ventral sternites, pleopods and gills remain incomplete. One selected female phenotype; no systematic age, moult or sexual dimorphism model. No inner distal carpal tooth has been copied from the shore crab.

surface.before: Nearly uniform green/blue material and generic body relief.
surface.changed: Original fine instanced granules, numerical chitin normal field, low olive mottling, blue plated limb surfaces, longitudinal palm ridge cues, rust female fingers and a pale ventral panel. Rim deformation was localized to remove visible radial flutes; the initial round paddle blades were elongated and pale front covers subdued.
surface.remaining: The photograph is a preserved museum specimen, not a live calibrated material or 3D scan. Pigment, wear, transparency and roughness are authored. Fine tooth/finger granularity and segment seams remain stylized; this is not photoreal metrology.

movement.before: Simple chela gesture and fixed generic limbs, without species-specific walking/P5 mechanisms.
movement.changed: A seven-second authored lateral walking bout with planted stance, lifted recovery and final hold. Independent P5 joint chains provide a stationary sideways-swim stroke study; leading/trailing walking-leg roles differ. Same body/materials support local handling, claw opening, low quiet support and Observe reset. A contact-classification defect that marked barely raised toes as planted was corrected.
movement.remaining: No imported joint trajectories, quantitative biological limits, calibrated gait timing, force, neural or fluid model. No calculated swim propulsion, prey contact, ingestion, sleep or male courtship. Three-dimensional biological articulation is more complex than the authored chains.

reviewMethod: Qualitative author comparison of60actual final main-viewer WebGL2 states plus three views of one actually exported static pose on nine labelled sheets. The reference is the authentic Wendy Kaveney / The Children’s Museum of Indianapolis female specimen photograph; selected FAO species diagnosis and diagrams were actually viewed, alongside retained Smithsonian SERC morphology and scoped indexed primary abstracts. No raw morphometric coordinates, gait trajectories or physiological measurements were fitted.
fixesAfterFirstRender: Localized shell teeth/spines to the rim, removing radial fan-like flutes.
Elongated the initially round P5 blades and retained their flattened propodus.
Made the broad female apron, narrowed telson cue and transverse creases visible in actual exported ventral review.
Fixed planted-contact classification for barely lifted walking toes.
